newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine parliament delays vote on tax breaks.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine parliament delays vote on tax breaks.

text.p: Ukraine's parliament on Friday delayed a vote for a week on a law which would re-institute tax breaks for foreign investors -- tax breaks the same parliament repealed at the end of April.

Deputies supported a motion by Viktor Suslov, head of the banking and finance committee, to demand an explanation as to why the government wanted the tax breaks repealed in the first place -- and why it wants them re-instituted now.

Suslov said previously Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko put pressure on parliament to pass the law, which would scrap breaks on taxes and customs duties to foreign investment joint ventures from July 1.
President Leonid Kuchma has asked parliament to re-institute a tax holiday until 1999 for foreign investment joint ventures started before January 1, 1995.
He also asked parliament this week to suggest a new law on breaks to businesses in the production sector.
Suslov said Ukraine went back on its word by changing the 994 guaranteeing the five-year tax holiday.

"The repeal of the breaks resulted in a sharp negative reaction on the part of investors and a pile of articles in the media, damaging not only the reputation of the prime minister but of all Ukraine," Suslov said.
The new law added to oft-repeated complaints by foreign investors of inconsistent laws, high taxes, and corruption.
Ukraine has attracted only $1.4 billion in foreign investment since independence almost six years ago.

Serhiy Tyhypko, appointed deputy prime minister in charge of the economy in April, has said the move was a mistake after he urged parliament to vote in favour of it it to recover an estimated $230-240 million in budget revenues.
